lessons.readingQ: What does Emma send to the manager?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a new situation with emails. What do you write? How do you start? What do you send? How do you end it?
lessons.speakingSample: I write a formal letter about a new job. I say, 'To whom it may concern, I am writing about the job.' I write a detailed letter. I talk about my previous job. I send a carbon copy to the manager. I write, 'Yours sincerely, Emma.' I like to write formal letters.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a new situation with emails. Say what you write and how you start and end it.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Lisa, I want to tell you about a new situation with emails. I write a formal letter about a new job. I say, 'To whom it may concern, I am writing about the job.' I write a detailed letter. I talk about my previous job. I send a carbon copy to the manager. I write, 'Yours sincerely, Emma.' I check the letter first. Best, Sam
lessons.sound: Previous has its strongest beat on PRE. In previous, say PRE clearly at the start. In detailed, say TAILED clearly at the end.
lessons.model: In the previous email, I asked about Friday.
lessons.wordSample: Her letter is about a new job.

transferCheck.source: Emma is a new colleague at Sam's office. On Monday, she writes a formal letter about a new job. Sam helps her. Emma says, 'To whom it may concern, I am writing about the job.' She writes a detailed letter about her previous job. She sends a carbon copy to the manager. She writes, 'Yours sincerely, Emma.' The manager reads the letter. Emma starts her new job on Monday. She is happy.
transferCheck.dictation: Emma writes a formal letter about a new job.
transferCheck.answer: 1. The new colleague is Emma. Sam helps her write a formal letter about a new job. 2. Emma starts her letter with 'To whom it may concern, I am writing about the job.' She does not know the name of the person. 3. Emma writes a detailed letter about her previous job. She sends a carbon copy to the manager. 4. Emma ends the letter with 'Yours sincerely, Emma.' The manager reads the letter. 5. Sample: On Monday, Emma writes a formal letter about a new job. Sam helps her. Emma says, 'To whom it may concern, I am writing about the job.' She writes a detailed letter about her previous job. She sends a carbon copy to the manager. She writes, 'Yours sincerely, Emma.' The manager reads the letter. Emma starts her new job on Monday. She is happy. Follow-up: When does Emma start her new job? She starts her new job on Monday.
